import numpy as np

def heuristics(demands, capacity):
    demands = np.asarray(demands, dtype=float)
    n = len(demands)
    
    # Create pairwise sum matrix
    pair_sum = demands[:, None] + demands[None, :]
    
    # Calculate waste for each pair
    waste = capacity - pair_sum
    
    # Identify valid pairs where sum <= capacity
    valid_mask = pair_sum <= capacity
    
    # Compute degree (number of valid partners) for each item
    # An item j can follow item i if demands[i] + demands[j] <= capacity
    # So for each item j, its degree is the number of items i such that demands[i] + demands[j] <= capacity
    # This is the number of True values in column j of valid_mask
    degrees = np.sum(valid_mask, axis=0)  # shape (n,)
    
    # Scarcity: inverse of degree + 1 (to avoid division by zero)
    # Items with fewer partners are more scarce/constrained
    scarcity = 1.0 / (degrees + 1.0)  # shape (n,)
    
    # Initialize heuristic matrix with a very small value for invalid pairs
    eta = np.full((n, n), 1e-9, dtype=float)
    
    # For valid pairs, combine fit quality with scarcity of the target item
    # Higher scarcity of j means we should place j sooner (it's more constrained)
    # Better fit (lower waste) is also better
    # We use: scarcity[j] / (waste + 1)
    # This rewards placing scarce items and good fits
    scarcity_matrix = scarcity[None, :]  # shape (1, n), broadcast over rows
    eta[valid_mask] = scarcity_matrix[valid_mask] / (waste[valid_mask] + 1.0)
    
    return eta
